summary: Time-boxed access to de-identified inference snippets for privacy validation of new redaction rules
description:
Issue summary:
Request from Applied ML (privacy team) for a short, auditable access window to a small, de-identified set of inference input/output pairs to validate a new automatic redaction transform.

Impact:
- Low production risk if handled per controls below, but the validation must use live workload distributions to catch edge-cases.
- Customer data sensitivity: potential PII in free-text prompts; must ensure strong redaction and minimal exposure.

Environment:
- Production inference traces (us-east) sampled during business hours for the past 72 hours.

Request details / Scope:
- Provide up to 250 inference records (input + output) containing examples where the new redaction logic triggered or was expected to trigger.
- Records must be de-identified using the approved pipeline: token-level masking, email/SSN regex scrub, and hash-only user/session IDs.
- Timebox: access for 48 hours from provisioning. After that, copies must be destroyed and S3 artifacts permanently deleted.
- Consumers: Applied ML (aisha.patel@redwood.com), Privacy Review (tbd), and one engineer from serving-runtime (liam.chen@redwood.com).

Data fields requested:
- request_id (hashed), user_id (hashed), timestamp, model_name, prompt_text (de-identified), model_output (de-identified), routing_metadata, inference_latency_ms.

Justification:
- New redaction transform introduced in PR #4521 needs validation against production prompt phrasing to confirm no PII leaks and acceptable false-positive rate.
- Prior staging tests missed a rare customer prompt pattern observed in prod.

Controls requested / proposed safeguards:
- Approved users only (listed above) with temporary IAM role (AssumeRole duration 1h; multiple assumes allowed during 48h window).
- Data stored in a dedicated S3 path with SSE-KMS; access limited to role principal.
- Artifact TTL enforced by lifecycle rule + manual verification of deletion by SRE after expiry.
- Audit log export of all S3 access and role assumes forwarded to Security (sec-audit@redwood.com).
- No local copies allowed on personal machines; only EC2 bastion with encrypted volume may be used for analysis.

Approvals required:
- Privacy Lead (Olivia Ramirez)
- Security (SRE lead: Marcus Holloway)
- Legal (if dataset contains >1 confirmed PII instance)

Deliverable format:
- NDJSON file with each line representing a single de-identified record.

Desired timeline:
- Approval decision within 48 hours (business days).
- Provisioning within 24 hours after approvals.

investigation_notes:
Sampling query run: SELECT top 1000 from inference_traces where timestamp >= now() - interval '72 hours' and model_name in ('redwood-2.7b','open-llm-v1') and redaction_score < 0.95 order by rand() limit 1000.
Initial checks:
- Confirmed 12 candidate prompts with email-like tokens and 3 with SSN-like patterns.
- Redaction pipeline (staging) applied token masking and regex scrub; confirmed no raw emails remain in the sample preview.
- KV-cache references were removed and session IDs replaced with HMAC-sha256(user_id, salt).
- Logs: audit log for sampling query recorded at https://splunk.redwood.com/en-US/app/search/jobs/7089123 (access restricted).
Hypothesis:
- New redaction thresholds are too conservative for short-form prompts, causing false negatives. Need production distribution to estimate precision/recall.
Open questions:
- Do we need to include model logits or only final output? (Privacy prefers no logits).
resolution:
Pending final privacy sign-off. Interim actions taken:
- SRE created timeboxed S3 path with SSE-KMS and lifecycle TTL 72 hours; KMS policy updated to allow assume-role for listed principals.
- Uploaded 5 de-identified sample records to the preview path for Privacy review.
- Security logged the permission change (ticket SEC-1142) and scheduled a follow-up audit.
Planned final steps after approval:
1) Run sanitized export job to produce NDJSON (max 250 records) into s3://redwood-internal-privacy-exports/INT-63249-<timestamp>.
2) Notify principals and hand off an IAM role with 48h window and 1h assume duration.
3) After 48h, SRE will verify deletion, run object-delete verification, and produce an audit report linking to this ticket.
4) If >1 confirmed PII instance found in the full set, Legal will be engaged and a wider remediation plan will be created.
Follow-ups / Action items:
- Update the data-extraction SOP to include HMAC-based user_id hashing as a mandatory step (owner: Applied ML).
- Add an automation to generate short-lived role credentials rather than manual creation (owner: SRE infra).
